column1: MULTI-FACTOR TESTING PROTOCOL - exact steps, in order, every time

column3: Only factors that individually PASSED Stage 2/3 of the Roadmap (real, purged, significant) enter the pool. Factors still in Stage 1 (collecting) or that FAILED Stage 2 are excluded, no matter how promising they look.
column4: This is the single biggest guard against the VIF-630 mistake - most bad combinations start with an ineligible factor included anyway.

column3: Try every combination of eligible factors, sizes 2 to 5, using fast Ridge regression on a coarse walk-forward (every 15-20 days, not every 5). This is intentionally cheap - hundreds/thousands of combos tested quickly to rank candidates.
column4: Output: ranked list by mean absolute error. Keep only the top 10-15 combos for the next step.

column3: Before any rigorous testing, compute VIF for every factor in each of the top 10-15 combos. Any combo with a factor VIF > 5 is DISCARDED immediately, even if it scored well in Step 2.
column4: This is a hard rule, not a judgment call. VIF>5 means the factors are measuring the same underlying thing - the earlier 630 VIF disaster happened because this check was skipped.

column3: Surviving combos go through PURGED, non-overlapping walk-forward validation using tree-based models (Random Forest / XGBoost - proven necessary since linear models underperform on this data). Report both the best combo's score AND the median of all surviving combos.
column4: If the median is much worse than the best, the best is probably lucky, not real. Trust the median-level performance, not the best-case number.

column3: For the winning combination: does the story make economic sense? (e.g. 'ingot demand leads scrap price by 2-3 weeks because mills buy scrap to feed billet production' is sensible; 'USD/INR 6-day-old value predicts 90-day price' is not, without a real mechanism.)
column4: Any factor that wins statistically but has no plausible mechanism gets flagged for extra scrutiny before being trusted - this is the human-judgment layer that pure search cannot replace.

column2: CALIBRATION TEST ON THE FINAL MODEL
column3: Before reporting any confidence band, run the calibration check: does the stated 80% band actually contain the true outcome ~80% of the time in the backtest? (We already proved tight bands FAIL this - do not skip this step again.)
column4: If calibration fails, WIDEN the band until it passes. Never report a band width that hasn't been calibration-tested.

column3: Write down: exact factors used, exact model type, exact accuracy/MAPE at each horizon, exact N (independent test count), exact date range tested. This becomes the frozen 'current best model' until Stage 6 monitoring flags a need to redo it.
column4: No silent changes. If the model changes, log why (new data, factor stopped working, etc.) in this same document.

column1: WHY EACH STEP EXISTS (lessons already paid for in this project):
- Step 1 exists because we once tested USD/INR alone with only 2 days of real data and got nonsense.
- Step 2/4 split (cheap then rigorous) exists because full rigorous testing on every combo would take hours per horizon.
- Step 3 (VIF) exists because the original 18-feature model had VIF up to 630 and backwards coefficients as a direct result.
- Step 4 median-vs-best exists because our first 60d "1.32% MAPE" result was optimistic - the true model-agnostic number was ~2.8%.
- Step 6 (calibration) exists because a "tight" 500-rupee band was tested and found to cover only ~40% of outcomes, not 80%.
